detail.body: ### What does this PR do? Add end-to-end native NVFP4 W4A4 training and rollout on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, demonstrated with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base DAPO using Megatron/Transformer Engine and vLLM. This contributes to Sophia's [low-precision roadmap #5972](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/5972), specifically **NVFP4 real quant** and **NVFP4 training in Megatron**. In brief: - **Training:** Transformer Engine runs selected routed-expert MLPs in NVFP4 with per-token activation scaling and dequantized backward. Persistent policy weights remain BF16, with full optimizer state. - **Weight synchronization:** following the trainer-side quantization boundary of #8287, the trainer exports the routed experts as NVFP4 with `moe: NVFP4` and `moe_activation: nvfp4_per_token` after each policy update. - **Rollout:** vLLM loads the NVFP4 expert weights and quantizes activations per token, matching training. Refit preserves the storage referenced by CUDA graphs. Attention and the configured boundary-layer MLPs remain BF16. The Qwen3 example keeps the first two and last four MLP layers in BF16 and applies NVFP4 to the remaining 42 routed-expert MLP layers. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: [NVFP4](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NVFP4), [roadmap #5972](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+5972+in%3Abody). - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`. Related work: #6455 targets ModelOpt/TRT-LLM synchronization; #6992 provides FSDP W4A8 simulation; #7895 targets DeepSeek MXFP4 on TE FP8; #7519 adds MXFP8 training and rollout. #8287 adds ModelOpt NVFP4 QAT with static activation scales; this PR adds native TE NVFP4 training with per-token activation scaling, on the same export path. ### Test Unit tests (CPU and GB200) pass; scoped Ruff, formatting and lockfile checks pass. The trainer-side export is bit-identical to vLLM's online `nvfp4_per_token` quantization, and 6-step runs on Qwen3-30B-A3B (8 × 4 GB200) and a small DeepSeek-V3-layout model pass. #### Long run BF16 and W4A4 runs of the example script below (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, DAPO, R3, token-level TIS) on 8 nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs, 700 steps with checkpoint resume across jobs. **W4A4 vs BF16:** **Training score (`critic/score/mean`)** **Entropy (`actor/entropy`)** **Train–rollout mismatch (`rollout_corr/kl`)** **Gradient norm (`actor/grad_norm`)** **Performance:** at matched response length, NVFP4 rollout generation is about 1.3× faster than BF16 once the mean response exceeds ~2.5k tokens, giving roughly 1.2× shorter end-to-end steps; NVFP4 training itself is still slower than BF16 in Transformer Engine. ### API and Usage Example With a Ray cluster running on eight nodes, provide model and dataset paths shared by all workers: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/shared/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base \ TRAIN_FILE=/shared/data/train.parquet \ TEST_FILE=/shared/data/validation.parquet \ EXP_NAME=qwen3-native-nvfp4 \ PRECISION_MODE=real_nvfp4 \ bash examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh ``` Use `PRECISION_MODE=bf16` for the baseline. NVFP4 training is enabled like FP8 training, through `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config` (`fp4: e2m1`, `fp4_recipe: nvfp4`, and `first_last_layers_bf16` with `num_layers_at_start_in_bf16` / `num_layers_at_end_in_bf16`), and rollout through `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.moe=NVFP4` with `moe_activation=nvfp4_per_token`, whose `ignore` list keeps the same layers in BF16; the trainer checks that the two agree. The example uses the standard verl PPO entry point, parquet datasets and built-in reward manager, with the DAPO recipe (clip-higher, token-level loss, dynamic sampling and the overlong penalty), R3 routing replay and token-level TIS. See [the example guide](https://github.com/zhangyimi/verl/blob/feat/native-nvfp4/examples/real_nvfp4/README.md) for configuration and runtime setup. ### Design & Code Changes - **Training precision:** the Megatron per-module recipe (attention BF16, routed-expert MLPs NVFP4, carved-out layers BF16) is generated from the configuration rather than maintained as a file. After model construction, the effective precision of every attention and expert linear layer is checked against it. Packed THD sequences use the TE alignment for FP4 as for FP8. - **Rollout config and refit:** `moe_activation=nvfp4_per_token` selects a compressed-tensors scheme (NVFP4 weights, fully dynamic NVFP4 inputs). The trainer quantizes the experts with its own Triton kernel, sharing one global scale across `gate_proj`/`up_proj`, bit-identical to vLLM's online `nvfp4_per_token` quantization. In vLLM the scheme selects FlashInfer TRT-LLM with per-token activations; refits load each bucket in place into the expert storage captured by CUDA graphs and post-process each MoE layer, so the extra memory is one MoE layer. - **Routing replay:** use vLLM’s native fused-MoE routing capture and align replay data with FP4 training padding. - **Runtime compatibility:** Transformer Engine 2.20.2 from the verl wheelhouse. No vLLM source patch is needed. The validated Megatron + vLLM stack uses: | Component | Version | |---|---| | PyTorch | 2.13 / CUDA 13 | | vLLM | 0.32.0 | | Transformers | 5.16.1 | | Megatron-Core | 0.19.2 | | Megatron-Bridge | 0.6.2 | | Transformer Engine | 2.20.2 | | FlashInfer | 0.7.0.post1 | | CUTLASS DSL / QuACK | 4.8.0 / 0.6.5 | SGLang end-to-end validation remains follow-up work. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Run the complete all-files pre-commit suite. Focused lint, formatting, shell and lockfile checks have passed. - [x] Add usage, design and runtime compatibility documentation. - [x] Add focused unit and end-to-end coverage. Project CI integration remains to be completed. - [x] Request project CI and review. - [x] Check recipe coordination: the recipe submodule reference is unchanged; no companion recipe PR is required. AI assistance: OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude assisted with implementation, testing and this PR description.

+# NVFP4 RL on Blackwell (experimental)
+
+Last updated: 10/28/2026
+
+This recipe trains the routed experts of an MoE model in real NVFP4 with Megatron and Transformer Engine,
+and serves the rollout in the same precision. Activations are quantized per token on both sides.
+Parameters stay BF16; attention, dense MLPs, shared experts, router, norms, embeddings and the LM head run
+in BF16.
+
+For NVFP4 fake-quantization training, see [NVFP4 QAT](nvfp4_qat.md). The rollout quantization interface
+shared by all formats is described in [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md).
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Blackwell (SM100) GPUs
+- Validated with PyTorch 2.13 / CUDA 13, Transformer Engine 2.20.2, Megatron-Core 0.19.2, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2
+  and vLLM 0.32.0 (`uv sync --frozen --extra megatron --extra vllm`)
+- Megatron backend, PP=1 without virtual pipeline parallelism
+- vLLM rollout with TP and EP=1 or EP=TP, the colocated `naive` checkpoint engine and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
+  CUDA graphs. Data-parallel EP, EPLB, context parallelism (DCP/PCP) and speculative decoding are not
+  supported.
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+actor_rollout_ref:
+  actor:
+    megatron:
+      override_transformer_config:
+        fp4: e2m1
+        fp4_recipe: nvfp4
+        first_last_layers_bf16: true
+        num_layers_at_start_in_bf16: 2   # whole decoder layers kept in BF16
+        num_layers_at_end_in_bf16: 4
+  rollout:
+    quantization:
+      moe: NVFP4
+      moe_activation: nvfp4_per_token   # activations quantized per token, as in training
+      ignore: ["re:.*layers\\.(0|1|44|45|46|47)\\.mlp\\.experts\\..*"]  # same layers, 48-layer model
+```
+
+- `fp4` applies only to the routed experts and cannot be combined with `qat`. Training quantizes their
+  activations per token in the forward pass and runs the backward GEMMs on the dequantized forward operands;
+  `NVTE_BACKWARD_OVERRIDE=high_precision` uses the BF16 operands instead.
+- The rollout must keep exactly the training BF16 layers; the trainer checks every exported expert weight
+  against them.
+- Transformer Engine reads its NVFP4 recipe from `NVTE_*` environment variables; the trainer rejects a
+  recipe that differs. See `examples/real_nvfp4/runtime_env.yaml`.
+- Routed experts are found by name, so the recipe is not tied to one architecture. It is validated on
+  Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and a small model with the DeepSeek-V3 layout (dense first layer, MLA,
+  shared expert).
+
+## Rollout
+
+`moe_activation: nvfp4_per_token` (vLLM's `quantization_config.moe.activation`) exports NVFP4 expert weights on the trainer side, bit-identical to vLLM's
+online `nvfp4_per_token` quantization, and runs them on FlashInfer's TRT-LLM MoE kernel with per-token
+activation scales. Refits load each bucket in place into the storage the CUDA graphs captured, so the extra
+memory is one MoE layer's post-processing. With rollout TP and EP off, each rank holds a slice of every
+expert and computes the per-token scale of the `down_proj` input over its slice, so results differ slightly
+from TP=1.
+
+## Mismatch
+
+Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, EP=4 on 4 GPUs, vLLM rollout TP=1, measured with the script in
+[qat.md](qat.md#measuring-the-mismatch):
+
+| Rollout | Training | Backend | k3_kl |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| NVFP4 MoE | NVFP4 QAT | FlashInfer CUTLASS (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00832 |
+| NVFP4 MoE, `nvfp4_per_token` | BF16 | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.01025 |
+| NVFP4 MoE, `nvfp4_per_token` | native NVFP4 | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00740 |
+
+## Example: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with DAPO
+
+[`examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh)
+runs DAPO with routing replay (R3) and token-level TIS on 8 nodes × 4 GB200, keeping the first two and last four
+of the 48 layers in BF16; `PRECISION_MODE=bf16` runs the same job in BF16. With a Ray cluster running:
+
+```bash
+MODEL_PATH=/shared/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base \
+TRAIN_FILE=/shared/data/train.parquet \
+TEST_FILE=/shared/data/validation.parquet \
+PRECISION_MODE=real_nvfp4 EXP_NAME=qwen3-nvfp4 NNODES=8 \
+  bash examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh
+```
+
+See the [example README](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/examples/real_nvfp4/README.md) for the
+dataset format, runtime environment and tests.
+
+### Results
+
+700 steps of NVFP4 and BF16 with the example script, on an earlier version of this integration (vLLM 0.29).
+
+![Training score](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0693c0b-6789-4285-8658-44a885d72a72)
+*`critic/score/mean`. Orange: NVFP4, red: BF16*
+
+![Entropy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e63b552c-fe9b-4b23-9751-62c38976732c)
+*`actor/entropy`. Orange: NVFP4, red: BF16*
+
+![Rollout-training mismatch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13131fe5-c670-41ea-91e1-68e5fff123ee)
+*`rollout_corr/kl`. Orange: NVFP4, red: BF16*
+
+![Gradient norm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b121c562-b6f7-4432-8a7e-ed5768d78e69)
+*`actor/grad_norm`. Orange: NVFP4, red: BF16*
+
+Results and observations:
+
+- The training score follows BF16 for the first ~450 steps and is lower afterwards.
+- The rollout–training mismatch is 0.003–0.01 with NVFP4, against about 0.0003 with BF16.
+- NVFP4 rollout generation is about 1.3× faster than BF16 once the mean response exceeds ~2.5k tokens, giving
+  roughly 1.2× shorter steps; NVFP4 training itself is still slower than BF16 in Transformer Engine.

+# Native NVFP4 training and rollout (experimental)
+
+This example trains Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with Megatron/Transformer Engine NVFP4
+and runs vLLM rollout in the matching NVFP4 precision. Training parameters stay
+BF16; each refit exports the routed experts as NVFP4 on the trainer side
+(`rollout.quantization.moe=NVFP4` with `moe_activation=nvfp4_per_token`), and vLLM reloads them into the
+storage its CUDA graphs captured.
+
+## Precision and supported configuration
+
+`actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.fp4=e2m1` (with
+`fp4_recipe=nvfp4`) runs the routed-expert MLPs in NVFP4 with per-token activation scaling, dequantized backward, and
+adaptive 4-over-6 disabled. The `nvfp4_per_token` rollout uses the same
+precision: NVFP4 expert weights and activations quantized per token by
+FlashInfer's TRT-LLM MoE kernel. Attention, router, norms, embeddings and the
+LM head remain BF16 on both sides.
+
+Megatron-Core's `first_last_layers_bf16` with `num_layers_at_start_in_bf16` and
+`num_layers_at_end_in_bf16` keeps whole decoder layers in BF16 during training; `rollout.quantization.ignore` must list the same
+routed-expert layers, which the trainer checks when it exports weights. This example keeps
+the first two and last four of 48 layers in BF16.
+
+Routed experts are found by their names (`mlp.experts`, unpacked or packed),
+as the trainer-side export does, so the integration is not tied to one
+architecture: dense MLP layers, shared experts and other attention types such
+as MLA stay BF16 on both sides. It has been validated on Qwen3-30B-A3B and,
+with a small random model, on the DeepSeek-V3 layout (dense first layer, MLA,
+shared expert). Training uses PP=1 without virtual pipeline parallelism, and
+rollout TP (`ROLLOUT_TP`, default 1) with EP=1 or EP=TP (`ROLLOUT_EP`), the
+colocated `naive` checkpoint engine, BF16 KV cache, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA
+graphs and no speculative decoding.
+
+## Installation
+
+The runtime uses PyTorch 2.13.0/CUDA 13, Transformer Engine 2.20.2,
+Megatron-Core 0.19.2, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2 and vLLM 0.32.0:
+
+```bash
+uv sync --frozen --extra megatron --extra vllm
+```
+
+## Run
+
+Use preprocessed datasets in verl's standard `RLHFDataset` format. Each row
+contains a `prompt` chat-message list, a `data_source` identifier and a
+`reward_model` mapping with `style: rule` and the answer in `ground_truth`.
+The built-in reward dispatcher selects scoring from `data_source`; use
+`math_dapo` for DAPO math or an `aime`-prefixed identifier for AIME. Optional
+`extra_info` is passed through by the dataset. Dataset preprocessing belongs
+outside this example; see the existing [preprocessing scripts](../data_preprocess).
+
+Start Ray on the allocated nodes, then provide shared model and parquet paths:
+
+```bash
+MODEL_PATH=/shared/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base \
+TRAIN_FILE=/shared/data/train.parquet \
+TEST_FILE=/shared/data/validation.parquet \
+CKPTS_DIR=/shared/checkpoints/my-run \
+PRECISION_MODE=real_nvfp4 EXP_NAME=my-run NNODES=8 \
+  bash examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh
+```
+
+Use `PRECISION_MODE=bf16` for a control with the same example settings. The
+launcher uses verl's standard PPO entry point with the built-in DAPO reward
+manager and the default rule-based scorer for each `data_source`. The default
+configuration is 8 nodes × 4 GPUs, EP=4, DAPO (GRPO advantages, clip-higher,
+token-level loss, dynamic sampling on accuracy and a 512-token overlong
+penalty), R3 routing replay and token-level TIS, training on 32 prompts × 16
+responses per update. Adam uses learning rate 1e-6 and betas (0.9, 0.999).
+
+Rollout memory utilization defaults to 0.8, with 256 sequences and 32768 batched
+tokens. Set `TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS`, `RESUME_MODE` and checkpoint paths for the
+run. Checkpoints include optimizer, scheduler and dataloader progress.
+Logging uses verl's standard console and W&B integration.
+
+Transformer Engine reads its NVFP4 settings from `NVTE_*` environment variables
+in each worker; `runtime_env.yaml` sets them and the trainer rejects a recipe
+that differs. Keep these variables when passing another file via `RUNTIME_ENV`.
+Only `NVTE_BACKWARD_OVERRIDE` may change: `dequantized` (the default here) runs
+the backward GEMMs on the dequantized forward operands, `high_precision` on the
+original BF16 ones.
+
+R3 uses vLLM's native routing capture inside the fused MoE path. Runtime checks
+validate the exported expert tensors, the NVFP4 layer selection and the scale
+values after each reload.
+
+## Tests
+
+Run GPU tests in a Blackwell allocation using the prepared runtime:
+
+```bash
+export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
+export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1 TRTLLM_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1
+python -m pytest -q tests/utils/real_nvfp4
+python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_bucketed_weight_transfer.py
+```
+
+Coverage includes recipe compatibility, the rollout preset, the in-place refit, and
+bit-exact agreement of the trainer-side export with vLLM's online NVFP4 quantization.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# DAPO training on Qwen3-30B-A3B with native W4A4 routed-expert MLPs,
+# per-token rollout activation scaling, and BF16 boundary-layer carve-outs:
+# GRPO advantages, clip-higher, token-level loss, dynamic sampling and the
+# overlong reward penalty.
+
+readonly PRECISION_MODE=${PRECISION_MODE:-real_nvfp4}
+case "$PRECISION_MODE" in
+  bf16|real_nvfp4) ;;
+  *) echo "PRECISION_MODE must be bf16 or real_nvfp4" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac
+readonly TRAIN_PROMPT_BSZ=32
+readonly N_RESP_PER_PROMPT=16
+readonly PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE=32
+readonly MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=20480
+readonly MAX_MODEL_LEN=21504
+readonly TRAIN_MAX_TOKEN_LEN=43008
+readonly OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN=512
+readonly MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS=32768
+readonly MAX_NUM_SEQS=256
+readonly AGENT_NUM_WORKERS=8
+
+readonly WORKING_DIR=${WORKING_DIR:-$PWD}
+readonly RAY_ADDRESS=${RAY_ADDRESS:-http://127.0.0.1:8265}
+readonly RUNTIME_ENV=${RUNTIME_ENV:-$WORKING_DIR/examples/real_nvfp4/runtime_env.yaml}
+readonly NNODES=${NNODES:-8}
+readonly N_GPUS_PER_NODE=${N_GPUS_PER_NODE:-4}
+# Per-token NVFP4 rollout supports ROLLOUT_EP=1 or ROLLOUT_EP=ROLLOUT_TP.
+readonly ROLLOUT_TP=${ROLLOUT_TP:-1}
+readonly ROLLOUT_EP=${ROLLOUT_EP:-$ROLLOUT_TP}
+readonly PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-verl-nvfp4}
+readonly EXP_NAME=${EXP_NAME:?set EXP_NAME to a new W&B/checkpoint run id}
+readonly RAY_DATA_HOME=${RAY_DATA_HOME:-$WORKING_DIR}
+readonly MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to your shared model directory}
+readonly TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:?set TRAIN_FILE to your preprocessed training parquet}
+readonly TEST_FILE=${TEST_FILE:?set TEST_FILE to your preprocessed validation parquet}
+readonly CKPTS_DIR=${CKPTS_DIR:-$RAY_DATA_HOME/checkpoints/$PROJECT_NAME/$EXP_NAME}
+readonly TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=${TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS:-20}
+readonly RESUME_MODE=${RESUME_MODE:-disable}
+readonly RESUME_FROM_PATH=${RESUME_FROM_PATH:-}
+
+[[ -f "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]]
+[[ -f "$TRAIN_FILE" && -f "$TEST_FILE" && -f "$RUNTIME_ENV" ]]
+[[ "$RESUME_MODE" = disable || "$RESUME_MODE" = auto || "$RESUME_MODE" = resume_path ]]
+if [[ "$RESUME_MODE" = resume_path ]]; then
+  [[ -d "$RESUME_FROM_PATH" && "$RESUME_FROM_PATH" = *global_step_* ]]
+else
+  [[ -z "$RESUME_FROM_PATH" ]]
+fi
+
+# Transformer Engine and FlashInfer read their NVFP4 settings from the worker
+# environment, which RUNTIME_ENV provides.
+
+DATA=(
+  data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILE"
+  data.val_files="$TEST_FILE"
+  data.prompt_key=prompt
+  data.return_raw_chat=True
+  data.truncation=left
+  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True
+  data.filter_overlong_prompts_workers=1
+  data.max_prompt_length=1024
+  data.max_response_length="$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH"
+  data.train_batch_size="$TRAIN_PROMPT_BSZ"
+)
+
+ALGORITHM=(
+  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo
+  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
+  algorithm.kl_ctrl.kl_coef=0.0
+  algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is=token
+  algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is_threshold=2.0
+  algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is_batch_normalize=False
+  algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_rs=null
+  algorithm.filter_groups.enable=True
+  algorithm.filter_groups.metric=acc
+)
+
+MODEL=(
+  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL_PATH"
+  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=False
+)
+
+ACTOR=(
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=False
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.0
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0.0
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=0.2
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=0.28
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_c=10.0
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size="$PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE"
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu="$TRAIN_MAX_TOKEN_LEN"
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_warmup_steps=0
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_decay_style=constant
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.weight_decay=0.1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.betas='[0.9,0.999]'
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.use_checkpoint_opt_param_scheduler=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.clip_grad=1.0
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_offload=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimizer_offload=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size=1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size=1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.expert_model_parallel_size=4
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.expert_tensor_parallel_size=1
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.sequence_parallel=False
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_mbridge=True
+  actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.router_replay.mode=R3
+  +actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.apply_rope_fusion=True
+  +actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.attention_dropout=0.0
+  +actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.hidden_dropout=0.0
+  +actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.moe_router_dtype=fp32
+  +actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.moe_token_dispatcher_type=alltoall

+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_export_matches_vllm_online_quantization_bitwise(dtype):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(17029)
+    num_experts, hidden, intermediate = 4, 256, 128
+    w13 = torch.randn((num_experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden), device="cuda", dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
+    w2 = torch.randn((num_experts, hidden, intermediate), device="cuda", dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
+    # Zero, tiny and large experts, and gate/up halves with different ranges.
+    for weight in (w13, w2):
+        weight[0].zero_()
+        weight[1].mul_(0.01)
+        weight[2].mul_(10)
+    w13[3, :intermediate].mul_(3)
+
+    prefix = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts"
+    stream = []
+    for expert in range(num_experts):
+        gate, up = w13[expert].split(intermediate)
+        stream += [
+            (f"{prefix}.{expert}.gate_proj.weight", gate.clone()),
+            (f"{prefix}.{expert}.down_proj.weight", w2[expert].clone()),
+            (f"{prefix}.{expert}.up_proj.weight", up.clone()),
+        ]
+    config = build_compressed_tensors_config(
+        linear=None, moe="NVFP4", moe_activation="nvfp4_per_token", ignore=[], config_file=None
+    )
+    out = dict(NVFP4PerTokenWeightQuantizer(config)(stream))
+
+    for stacked, projections in ((w13, ("gate_proj", "up_proj")), (w2, ("down_proj",))):
+        packed, block_scale, weight_scale_2 = nvfp4._quantize_moe_weight_to_nvfp4(stacked)
+        for expert in range(num_experts):
+            names = [f"{prefix}.{expert}.{projection}" for projection in projections]
+            got_packed = torch.cat([out[f"{name}.weight_packed"] for name in names])
+            got_scale = torch.cat([out[f"{name}.weight_scale"] for name in names])
+            assert torch.equal(got_packed, packed[expert])
+            assert got_scale.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+            assert torch.equal(got_scale.view(torch.uint8), block_scale[expert].view(torch.uint8))
+            for name in names:
+                # vLLM's compressed-tensors loader stores the reciprocal of the exported global scale.
+                assert torch.equal(1.0 / out[f"{name}.weight_global_scale"], weight_scale_2[expert].reshape(1))
+                assert torch.equal(out[f"{name}.input_global_scale"].cpu(), torch.ones(1))

+"""Per-token NVFP4 rollout refit on small Qwen3-MoE and DeepSeek-V3 models.
+
+The preset engine refits from the trainer-side export in place, as the rollout does.
+Its greedy logprobs must equal vLLM's online nvfp4_per_token method loading the same BF16
+weights, and with CUDA graphs a refit must restore them exactly, including after other
+weights and after a level-2 sleep.

+
+import gc
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
+pytest.importorskip("compressed_tensors")
+pytest.importorskip("vllm")
+
+from verl.utils.qat.compressed_tensors import (  # noqa: E402
+    NVFP4PerTokenWeightQuantizer,
+    build_compressed_tensors_config,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10,
+    reason="Per-token NVFP4 rollout needs a Blackwell (SM100) GPU",
+)
+
+NUM_LAYERS = 3
+PROMPTS = [[11, 523, 97, 1024, 7], [3, 3, 3, 900, 41, 2049], [1500, 8, 77]]
+
+
+def _qwen3_moe():
+    from transformers import Qwen3MoeConfig, Qwen3MoeForCausalLM
+
+    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
+        vocab_size=4096,
+        hidden_size=2048,
+        intermediate_size=6144,
+        moe_intermediate_size=768,
+        num_hidden_layers=NUM_LAYERS,
+        num_attention_heads=32,
+        num_key_value_heads=4,
+        head_dim=128,
+        num_experts=32,
+        num_experts_per_tok=8,
+        decoder_sparse_step=1,
+        norm_topk_prob=True,
+        max_position_embeddings=1024,
+        torch_dtype="bfloat16",
+    )
+    return Qwen3MoeForCausalLM(config)
+
+
+def _deepseek_v3():
+    # A dense first layer, MLA attention and a shared expert next to the routed ones.
+    from transformers import DeepseekV3Config, DeepseekV3ForCausalLM
+
+    config = DeepseekV3Config(
+        vocab_size=4096,
+        hidden_size=2048,
+        intermediate_size=6144,
+        moe_intermediate_size=768,
+        num_hidden_layers=NUM_LAYERS,
+        first_k_dense_replace=1,
+        num_attention_heads=16,
+        num_key_value_heads=16,

+        kv_lora_rank=512,

+        topk_method="noaux_tc",

+        topk_group=1,
+        norm_topk_prob=True,

+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=[_qwen3_moe, _deepseek_v3], ids=["qwen3_moe", "deepseek_v3"])
+def model_dir(request, tmp_path_factory):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = request.param().to(torch.bfloat16)
+    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(request.param.__name__)

+def _weights(model_dir, scale=1.0):
+    from safetensors import safe_open
+
+    out = []
+    for name in sorted(os.listdir(model_dir)):
+        if name.endswith(".safetensors"):
+            with safe_open(os.path.join(model_dir, name), "pt", device="cuda") as f:
+                for key in f.keys():
+                    tensor = f.get_tensor(key)
+                    out.append((key, tensor * scale if ".experts." in key else tensor))
+    return out

+def _engine(model_dir, eager, **kwargs):
+    from vllm import LLM
+
+    return LLM(
+        model=model_dir,
+        skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        max_model_len=256,
+        max_num_seqs=4,
+        # Small models: several engines run one after another in this process.
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.08,
+        enforce_eager=eager,
+        compilation_config=None if eager else {"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"},
+        enable_flashinfer_autotune=False,
+        seed=0,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _runner(llm):
+    core = llm.llm_engine.engine_core
+    core = getattr(core, "engine_core", core)
+    return core.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
+
+
+def _refit(llm, weights):
+    """The rollout worker's quantized refit, in buckets of 32 tensors."""
+    from verl.utils.vllm.vllm_quant_utils import (
+        load_quanted_weights,
+        prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading,
+        process_quanted_weights_after_loading,
+    )
+
+    runner = _runner(llm)
+    model = runner.get_model()
+    reload_state = prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading(model)
+    for start in range(0, len(weights), 32):
+        load_quanted_weights(weights[start : start + 32], runner)
+    process_quanted_weights_after_loading(model, reload_state)
+
+
+def _logprobs(llm):
+    from vllm import SamplingParams
+
+    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=16, logprobs=0)
+    outputs = llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": p} for p in PROMPTS], params, use_tqdm=False)
+    return [[next(iter(lp.values())).logprob for lp in o.outputs[0].logprobs] for o in outputs]
+
+
+def _kv_caches(llm):
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention_layer_base import AttentionLayerBase
+
+    caches = []
+    for module in _runner(llm).get_model().modules():
+        if isinstance(module, AttentionLayerBase):
+            kv = getattr(module, "kv_cache", None)
+            caches.extend(t for t in (kv if isinstance(kv, list | tuple) else [kv]) if isinstance(t, torch.Tensor))
+    return caches
+
+
+def _free():
+    # Callers drop their engine reference first: shutting an engine down tears down
+    # vLLM's process-wide parallel state, which the next engine would otherwise lose.
+    gc.collect()
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+

+def test_preset_refit_matches_online_quantization(model_dir, request):
+    from verl.utils.vllm.vllm_nvfp4_per_token_utils import (
+        attest_nvfp4_per_token_runtime,
+        clear_kv_cache,
+        nvfp4_per_token_quantization_config,
+        routed_expert_layers,
+    )
+    from verl.utils.vllm.vllm_quant_utils import apply_vllm_quant_patches
+
+    carved = [0, NUM_LAYERS - 1]
+    # vLLM's online method quantizes the BF16 checkpoint at load. Eager mode keeps the
+    # comparison independent of each engine's KV-cache size, which steers graph kernels.
+    online = _engine(
+        model_dir,
+        eager=True,
+        quantization="nvfp4_per_token",
+        quantization_config={"ignore": [f"model.layers.{i}.mlp.experts" for i in carved]},
+        moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm",
+    )
+    expected = _logprobs(online)
+    del online
+    _free()
+
+    apply_vllm_quant_patches()
+    ignore = [r"re:.*layers\.(" + "|".join(map(str, carved)) + r")\.mlp\.experts\..*"]
+    config = build_compressed_tensors_config(
+        linear=None, moe="NVFP4", moe_activation="nvfp4_per_token", ignore=ignore, config_file=None
+    )
+
+    def refit(llm, scale):
+        model = _runner(llm).get_model()
+        layers = routed_expert_layers(model, config)
+        assert sorted(layer for layer, (_, quantized) in layers.items() if quantized) == [1]
+        _refit(llm, list(NVFP4PerTokenWeightQuantizer(config)(_weights(model_dir, scale))))
+        attest_nvfp4_per_token_runtime(model, config)
+        return _logprobs(llm)
+
+    preset = _engine(model_dir, eager=True, load_format="dummy", hf_overrides={"quantization_config": config})
+    # The worker finds the per-token config that came in through hf_overrides.
+    assert nvfp4_per_token_quantization_config(_runner(preset).vllm_config) is not None
+    # Start-up forwards with the dummy weights can leave NaN in the KV cache; the rollout
+    # clears it once the engine is up (monkey_patch_model).
+    clear_kv_cache(_runner(preset).get_model())
+    assert _kv_caches(preset) and all(torch.isfinite(t).all() for t in _kv_caches(preset))
+    assert refit(preset, 1.0) == expected
+    del preset
+    _free()
+
+    # vLLM allows one sleep-mode (CuMem) engine per process, so one model covers the sleep.
+    sleep = request.node.callspec.id == "qwen3_moe"
+    preset = _engine(
+        model_dir,
+        eager=False,
+        load_format="dummy",
+        enable_sleep_mode=sleep,
+        hf_overrides={"quantization_config": config},
+    )
+    first = refit(preset, 1.0)
+    assert refit(preset, 1.5) != first
+    assert refit(preset, 1.0) == first
+    if sleep:

+        preset.sleep(level=2)
+        preset.wake_up()
+        assert refit(preset, 1.0) == first
+    del preset
+    _free()

+def bf16_layers_at_start_end(override_transformer_config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Decoder layers Megatron-Core keeps in BF16 at the start and end (``first_last_layers_bf16``)."""
+    if not override_transformer_config.get("first_last_layers_bf16", False):
+        return 0, 0
+    # Megatron-Core defaults
+    start = override_transformer_config.get("num_layers_at_start_in_bf16", 1)
+    end = override_transformer_config.get("num_layers_at_end_in_bf16", 1)
+    if start < 0 or end < 0:

+    return start, end

+    """Decoder layers kept in BF16 by the first/last carve-out."""

+"""Engine-neutral NVFP4 weight packing for trainer-side export.
+
+:func:`quantize_nvfp4` follows the arithmetic of the CUDA NVFP4 quantization kernel the
+inference engines share (vLLM ``scaled_fp4_quant``, which vLLM's online NVFP4 methods use):
+16-element blocks, an E4M3 block scale ``global_scale * amax / 6`` and round-to-nearest-even
+E2M1 values. The kernel computes reciprocals with ``rcp.approx.ftz.f32``, so this Triton
+kernel does too; a GPU test checks it bitwise against vLLM.

+import triton
+import triton.language as tl

+__all__ = ["quantize_nvfp4"]
+
+_BLOCK = 16
+
+

+def _rcp_approx(x):
+    return tl.inline_asm_elementwise("rcp.approx.ftz.f32 $0, $1;", "=f,f", [x], dtype=tl.float32, is_pure=True, pack=1)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _e2m1_code(x):
+    # Round-to-nearest-even onto {0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6}, saturating at 6.
+    a = tl.abs(x)
+    code = tl.where(
+        a <= 0.25,
+        0,
+        tl.where(
+            a < 0.75,
+            1,
+            tl.where(
+                a <= 1.25,
+                2,
+                tl.where(a < 1.75, 3, tl.where(a <= 2.5, 4, tl.where(a < 3.5, 5, tl.where(a <= 5.0, 6, 7)))),
+            ),
+        ),
+    )
+    # The sign bit survives rounding to zero, as in the hardware conversion.
+    sign = tl.where(x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) < 0, 8, 0)
+    return (code + sign).to(tl.uint8)
+

+    x_ptr,
+    packed_ptr,
+    scale_ptr,
+    global_scale_ptr,
+    M,
+    N,
+    stride_xm,
+    TILE_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCKS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0) * TILE_M + tl.arange(0, TILE_M)
+    blocks = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCKS + tl.arange(0, BLOCKS)
+    cols = blocks[:, None] * 16 + tl.arange(0, 16)[None, :]

+
+import fnmatch
+from typing import Any, Mapping
+
+from verl.utils.megatron.low_precision import bf16_layer_indices, hf_config_get, text_config
+
+# Megatron module paths of routed-expert GEMMs (grouped or sequential experts). Dense MLPs
+# (``mlp.linear_fc1``) and shared experts (``mlp.shared_experts.linear_fc1``) do not match.
+ROUTED_EXPERT_PATTERNS = ("*.mlp.experts.*linear_fc1", "*.mlp.experts.*linear_fc2")
+
+
+def is_routed_expert_module(module_path: str) -> bool:
+    """Return whether a Megatron module path identifies a routed-expert GEMM."""
+
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(module_path, pattern) for pattern in ROUTED_EXPERT_PATTERNS)
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_enabled(override_transformer_config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``override_transformer_config.fp4`` trains the routed experts in NVFP4.
+
+    NVFP4 training is switched on by ``fp4``, as FP8 training is by ``fp8``; it applies
+    to routed-expert GEMMs only.
+    """
+
+    fp4 = override_transformer_config.get("fp4")
+    if not fp4:
+        return False
+    fp4_recipe = override_transformer_config.get("fp4_recipe") or "nvfp4"
+    if fp4 != "e2m1" or fp4_recipe != "nvfp4":
+        raise ValueError(f"FP4 training supports fp4='e2m1' with fp4_recipe='nvfp4', got {fp4!r}/{fp4_recipe!r}")
+    return True
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_quant_recipe_config(num_layers: int, num_layers_at_start: int, num_layers_at_end: int) -> dict:
+    """Megatron-Core per-module recipe: routed-expert GEMMs NVFP4, everything else BF16.
+
+    The result is passed to ``RecipeConfig.from_config_dict``. MCore takes the
+    first matching matcher, so the carved-out layers precede the expert
+    patterns, and a final catch-all keeps attention, dense MLPs and shared
+    experts in BF16: a TE module no matcher selects would inherit the layer's
+    FP4 autocast. Layer indices in module paths are global only with PP=1,
+    which :func:`validate_real_nvfp4_parallelism` enforces.
+    """
+
+    def glob(config: str, pattern: str) -> dict:
+        return {"config": config, "type": "glob", "pattern": pattern, "enabled": True}
+
+    matchers = {
+        f"layer_{index}_bf16": glob("bf16", f"*.layers.{index}.*")
+        for index in bf16_layer_indices(num_layers, num_layers_at_start, num_layers_at_end)
+    }
+    matchers["experts_fc1_nvfp4"] = glob("nvfp4", ROUTED_EXPERT_PATTERNS[0])
+    matchers["experts_fc2_nvfp4"] = glob("nvfp4", ROUTED_EXPERT_PATTERNS[1])
+    matchers["other_bf16"] = glob("bf16", "*")
+    return {
+        "configs": {
+            "bf16": {"transformer_engine_config_type": "TEQuantizationParams", "training_recipe": {}},
+            "nvfp4": {
+                "transformer_engine_config_type": "TEQuantizationParams",
+                # Enter NVFP4 even outside an FP4 autocast: some decoder blocks, such as
+                # Megatron-Bridge's Qwen3-VL block, only open FP8 contexts.
+                "training_recipe": {"fp4_quantization_recipe": "nvfp4", "override_nonquantized_autocast": True},
+            },
+        },
+        "matchers": matchers,
+    }
+
+
+def validate_real_nvfp4_model_contract(hf_config: Any) -> None:
+    """real_nvfp4 trains routed experts in NVFP4, so the model must have them."""
+
+    decoder = text_config(hf_config)
+    num_experts = int(hf_config_get(decoder, "num_experts") or hf_config_get(decoder, "n_routed_experts") or 0)
+    if num_experts <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "real_nvfp4 requires a routed-expert MoE model; this config declares no experts "
+            "(looked for num_experts / n_routed_experts)"
+        )
+
+
+def validate_real_nvfp4_parallelism(*, pipeline_size: int, virtual_pipeline_size: int | None) -> None:
+    """Keep layer-index recipes and rank-local attestation within the PP=1 scope."""
+
+    if pipeline_size != 1 or virtual_pipeline_size not in (None, 1):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "real_nvfp4 currently requires pipeline_model_parallel_size=1 and no virtual pipeline splitting; "
+            "layer precision and local attestation use global layer indices, got pp="
+            f"{pipeline_size} vpp={virtual_pipeline_size}"
+        )
+
+
+BACKWARD_OVERRIDES = ("dequantized", "high_precision")
+
+
+def validate_real_nvfp4_te_recipe(recipe: Any) -> None:
+    """Validate the effective Transformer Engine NVFP4 recipe.
+
+    TE reads these fields from ``NVTE_*`` environment variables when the recipe
+    is constructed, so this catches a worker started without them. Backward
+    GEMMs may use the dequantized forward operands or the high-precision ones
+    (``NVTE_BACKWARD_OVERRIDE``); every other field is fixed.
+    """
+
+    expected = {
+        "row_scaled_activation": True,
+        "disable_rht": True,
+        "disable_stochastic_rounding": True,
+        "disable_2d_quantization": True,
+        # The per-token NVFP4 rollout uses standard NVFP4, not TE's
+        # adaptive 4-over-6 representation. Keep training aligned.
+        "nvfp4_4over6": "none",
+        "nvfp4_4over6_e4m3_use_256": "all",
+        "nvfp4_4over6_err_mode": "MAE",
+    }
+    mismatches = {
+        name: {"expected": wanted, "actual": getattr(recipe, name, None)}
+        for name, wanted in expected.items()
+        if getattr(recipe, name, None) != wanted
+    }
+    for group_name in ("fp4_quant_fwd_inp", "fp4_quant_fwd_weight", "fp4_quant_bwd_grad"):
+        group = getattr(recipe, group_name, None)
+        for field_name in ("random_hadamard_transform", "stochastic_rounding", "fp4_2d_quantization"):
+            actual = getattr(group, field_name, None)
+            if actual is not False:
+                mismatches[f"{group_name}.{field_name}"] = {"expected": False, "actual": actual}
+    backward_override = getattr(recipe, "backward_override", None)
+    if backward_override not in BACKWARD_OVERRIDES:
+        mismatches["backward_override"] = {"expected": BACKWARD_OVERRIDES, "actual": backward_override}
+    if mismatches:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"real_nvfp4 Transformer Engine recipe drifted: {mismatches}")
+
+
+def check_nvfp4_per_token_rollout(
+    rollout_config: Any, quantization_config: Any, compilation_config: dict, engine_kwargs: dict
+) -> None:
+    """Keep a per-token NVFP4 rollout to the validated layout: no all2all expert
+    parallelism, colocated IPC refit and full CUDA graphs for decode only.
+
+    A no-op for other quantization configs, from ``rollout.quantization`` or the checkpoint.
+    """
+    from verl.utils.qat.compressed_tensors import is_nvfp4_per_token_config
+
+    if not is_nvfp4_per_token_config(quantization_config):
+        return
+    dp = rollout_config.data_parallel_size
+    # verl runs per-token NVFP4 on the monolithic FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel,
+    # which has no all2all expert dispatch.
+    if dp != 1 or engine_kwargs.get("enable_eplb", False):
+        raise ValueError(f"Per-token NVFP4 rollout requires data_parallel_size=1 and no EPLB, got dp={dp}")
+    # DCP cannot run FULL CUDA graphs, and PCP turns expert parallelism into all2all.
+    context_parallel = {
+        key: engine_kwargs.get(key, 1) or 1 for key in ("decode_context_parallel_size", "prefill_context_parallel_size")
+    }
+    if any(size > 1 for size in context_parallel.values()):
+        raise ValueError(f"Per-token NVFP4 rollout does not support context parallelism, got {context_parallel}")
+    mtp = rollout_config.mtp
+    if mtp is not None and mtp.enable and mtp.enable_rollout:
+        raise ValueError("Per-token NVFP4 rollout does not support speculative decoding/MTP")
+    checkpoint_backend = getattr(rollout_config.checkpoint_engine, "backend", None)
+    if checkpoint_backend != "naive":
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Per-token NVFP4 refits through the colocated naive IPC checkpoint backend, got {checkpoint_backend!r}"
+        )
+    compilation_config.setdefault("cudagraph_mode", "FULL_DECODE_ONLY")
+    if compilation_config["cudagraph_mode"] != "FULL_DECODE_ONLY":
+        raise ValueError("Per-token NVFP4 rollout requires compilation_config['cudagraph_mode']=FULL_DECODE_ONLY")

+    """

+    fp4_recipe = getattr(tf_config.fp4_recipe, "value", tf_config.fp4_recipe)

+    for model in models:

@ISEEKYAN  Thanks for your comments!  
1. The KL in nvfp4(rollout+training) is clearly higher than bf16. It keeps training relatively stable, but in longer runs nvfp4 is more likely than bf16 to crash first. That is why we keep some layers in bf16.

    nvfp4 rollout + bf16 training crashes earlier due to the train-infer precision mismatch, so training needs QAT at least. But even with QAT, it performed worse than nvfp4 (rollout + training) in our tests.

    The impact of the nvfp4 train-infer mismatch is still an open problem. Our work [TRIAGE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07043)  and others such as [TRACE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07767) are working on it. This PR provides the basic NVFP4 training and rollout support that such methods can build on.

2. We keep the first 2 and last 4 layers in bf16 based on experience. In our experiments, quantizing all layers made training less stable. This setting is configurable and can be changed for other models.

## Megatron / trainer-side refactor

The latest change to enable native NVFP4 through `override_transformer_config.fp4/fp4_recipe` is directionally consistent with FP8/MXFP8. However, the internal abstraction is still NVFP4-specific and should be consolidated before this becomes a public low-precision API.

1. **Replace the preset-to-QAT-mode map with a typed precision descriptor.** `SUPPORTED_SCHEMES` currently mixes checkpoint wire format, QAT compatibility, activation scaling, target scope, and backend capability; `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN: None` is evidence that one map no longer represents the contract. A common descriptor should drive config construction, QAT/native-training compatibility, exporter selection, rollout adapter selection, and validation for FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4/NVFP4.

2. **Do not alias `NVFP4` and `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` as the same numerical preset.** The existing NVFP4 QAT path exports an observed/static `input_global_scale`, while native TE NVFP4 uses per-token dynamic activation scaling and exports `input_global_scale=1` only as checkpoint metadata. They also select different kernels. A unified public shape such as `NVFP4 + activation_scaling={static, per_token}` would be reasonable, but silently mapping ModelOpt QAT to `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` would break the training/rollout numerical-contract check.

3. **Single-source the BF16 carve-out.** Training derives it from `first_last_layers_bf16` and `num_layers_at_{start,end}_in_bf16`, while rollout requires users to repeat the same layers as a hand-written `quantization.ignore` regex. The current code only validates that the two copies agree. Please build a common low-precision plan that generates the Megatron `quant_recipe`, rollout ignore rules, exporter targets, and runtime attestation expectations from one source. The validation probe in `_check_real_nvfp4_carveout` should also use canonical exported names rather than the hard-coded `model.layers.{i}.mlp.experts...` prefix.

4. **Keep the trainer-side exporter engine-neutral.** `NVFP4PerTokenWeightQuantizer._quantize` imports the private `vllm._custom_ops.scaled_fp4_quant`. This makes a Megatron actor depend on an inference-engine implementation and conflicts with the trainer/exporter/rollout boundary described in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. The packing implementation should live in an engine-neutral quantization backend, with a bitwise golden test against vLLM retained for compatibility.

5. **Narrow generic FP4 handling.** `get_thd_quant_align_size` currently returns 16 for any truthy `config.fp4`; at minimum it should check the supported NVFP4 recipe, otherwise future FP4 recipes inherit NVFP4 padding semantics accidentally.

6. **Dependency integration should follow project packaging.** `pyproject.toml` still switches Megatron to the PyPI TE 2.18 build, while the project wheelhouse update mentioned in the existing review targets TE 2.20.2. Please rebase the dependency change onto the wheelhouse-supported version rather than introducing a separate TE installation path here.

A useful target abstraction would be a `LowPrecisionPlan`/preset descriptor consumed by trainer adapters (`QAT`, `TE native`) and by the canonical `WeightQuantizer`, rather than passing `real_nvfp4_bf16_layers` as an NVFP4-specific argument through the generic dispatcher.

## vLLM / rollout-side refactor

The per-token path is numerically coherent and the scale-pointer attestations are useful, but it currently forms a second, NVFP4-specific refit stack beside the common FP8/MXFP4/NVFP4 path.

1. **Fold layerwise reload into the common quantized-refit lifecycle.** `update_weights_from_ipc` early-returns to `_update_nvfp4_per_token_weights`, bypassing `prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading`, the normal bucket loader, and `process_quanted_weights_after_loading`. This duplicates tied-alias handling, buffer handling, failure state, post-load processing, and feature restrictions. Please introduce a refit strategy interface such as `prepare/load_bucket/finalize/abort/attest`, selected by quantization capabilities. FP8, MXFP4, static NVFP4, and per-token NVFP4 should share the IPC/control flow and differ only in their strategy.

2. **Fail closed for inference after a partial refit.** The current exception path marks `_nvfp4_per_token_update_failed` and blocks the next refit, but the worker can still contain a mix of old and new layer weights. The unhealthy state should also reject decode requests or terminate/restart the worker; guarding only the next update is not a complete fail-closed contract.

3. **Minimize the vLLM monkey patch surface.** `vllm_nvfp4_per_token_utils.py` currently owns private-class replacement, kernel construction, checkpoint-layout conversion, reload behavior, scale-reference repair, and KV-cache cleanup. The compressed-tensors per-token MoE method should ideally be upstreamed to vLLM. verl should retain capability detection, the refit adapter, and compatibility guards. Also replace `type(...).__name__` detection with an explicit marker/protocol or an `isinstance` check against the registered method.

4. **Strengthen refit validation.** `NVFP4PerTokenRefitCheck` checks coverage and scale semantics, but not every incoming tensor's shape/dtype against the live/checkpoint-layout parameter. The generic quantized paths already perform stronger staging checks; the per-token strategy should reuse the same validation mechanism.

5. **Represent backend limitations as capabilities, not scattered preset checks.** `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` currently requires vLLM, TP/EP/PP=1, the `naive` checkpoint backend, no rollout MTP, and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. These should be declared by the rollout adapter and validated centrally. Please also explicitly decide and validate DCP support. With TP/EP/PP=1 this path is not production-ready for large MoE rollout, so the docs/API should call it experimental until the parallel refit path exists.

6. **Keep preset detection independent of where vLLM stores the effective config.** The server correctly checks the effective config after applying `hf_overrides`, but the worker derives the per-token config only from `model_config.hf_config.quantization_config`. Please add a focused startup test proving this field is populated for rollout overrides in the pinned vLLM version, or fall back to `vllm_config.quant_config`/the effective serialized config. Otherwise the worker can accidentally enter the generic refit path.

The desired end state is one generic rollout weight-sync pipeline with a `QuantizedRefitStrategy` selected from a structured precision descriptor. `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` should contribute a vLLM adapter, not another worker-level control flow.

@wuxibin89 Thanks for the detailed review.

> **1. Replace the preset-to-QAT-mode map with a typed precision descriptor.**

Agreed. It reshapes the FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4/NVFP4 paths together, so could we do it in a separate PR rather than in this one?

> **2. Do not alias `NVFP4` and `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` as the same numerical preset.**

They stay separate presets. We'll add an explicit `nvfp4_per_token` QAT mode for `NVFP4_PER_TOKEN` in a follow-up PR, so the static `nvfp4` QAT mode is never mapped to it. Folding both into `NVFP4` + `activation_scaling` can follow the descriptor in (1).

> **3. Single-source the BF16 carve-out.**

In 1c2e4d39 the exporter checks the carve-out on every exported routed-expert weight by its exported name, replacing the hard-coded `model.layers.{i}...` probe. Generating the rollout ignore and the Megatron recipe from one source fits best into the descriptor in (1).

> **4. Keep the trainer-side exporter engine-neutral.**

Done in 46b66bc6. The exporter packs NVFP4 with its own Triton kernel instead of `vllm._custom_ops.scaled_fp4_quant`; a GPU test checks it bitwise against vLLM.

> **5. Narrow generic FP4 handling.**

Done in 1c2e4d39. `get_thd_quant_align_size` returns 16 only for the `nvfp4` recipe and raises for other FP4 recipes.

> **6. Dependency integration should follow project packaging.**

We'll switch to the wheelhouse TE 2.20.2 once the cu130 build is published.

@wuxibin89

> **1. Fold layerwise reload into the common quantized-refit lifecycle.**

Agreed. It changes the refit flow of every quantized format and needs all of them re-validated, so could we do it in a separate PR?

> **2. Fail closed for inference after a partial refit.**

Done in 46b66bc6. After a partial refit the worker refuses to execute the model as well as any further refit.

> **3. Minimize the vLLM monkey patch surface.**

The method checks now use `isinstance` against the installed class (1c2e4d39). We plan to move the per-token method upstream, building on vLLM's online `nvfp4_per_token` and its NVFP4 re-quantization API, and slim the patch down once it lands.

> **4. Strengthen refit validation.**

Done in 1c2e4d39. Every incoming expert tensor is checked for shape and dtype against its checkpoint layout.

> **5. Represent backend limitations as capabilities, not scattered preset checks.**

Rollout TP is now supported with or without EP, validated on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Data-parallel EP and EPLB remain unsupported, as vLLM runs per-token NVFP4 only on the monolithic FlashInfer TRT-LLM path. DCP/PCP are rejected, and the docs mark the path experimental (1c2e4d39). Declaring these as adapter capabilities fits with (1).

> **6. Keep preset detection independent of where vLLM stores the effective config.**

Done in 1c2e4d39. The worker reads vLLM's built quant config and falls back to the HF config; a GPU test checks the `hf_overrides` case.
